concepts.title: Letters as Communication: Types and Purposes
concepts.definition: Letters bridge distance between people, and their form follows their purpose: personal letters to family and friends move between affection and news, while business and official letters -- enquiries, orders, complaints, applications -- follow fixed conventions because they are addressed to strangers and institutions.
concepts.key_idea: Write to the relationship -- warm and free with friends, formal and exact with strangers.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehb115.txt opening (letters between distant people, informal letters, formal letters, purposes of letter writing)
question_patterns: what are the main types of letters and their purposes

what purposes can a letter serve in daily life

solution_steps.explain: Ask who will read it -- a dear one or an office -- since that decides tone and format.
News and affection suit personal letters; enquiries, orders, complaints and applications demand formal shape.
Formal letters carry addresses, dates, salutations of title and signed designation; personal letters need only warmth and clarity.

concepts.title: Formal Letters: Layout and Conventions
concepts.definition: A formal letter follows a strict layout: writer's address and date, receiver's address, a formal salutation, a subject line stating the matter in a phrase, an organised body -- purpose, details, expectation of action -- and a courteous close with signature and name.
concepts.key_idea: Address, subject, body, close -- the formal letter's four-step etiquette leaves nothing to guesswork.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehb115.txt formal letter sections (layout, sender address, date, receiver address, subject line, salutation, complimentary close, signature)
question_patterns: describe the layout of a formal letter

write an application to the principal for leave using the correct format
where do the writer's and receiver's addresses go in a formal letter
draft a complaint letter about a defective product

solution_steps.explain: Place writer's address and date at the top, then the receiver's designation and address.
Open with a formal salutation and a crisp subject line; the first paragraph announces the purpose.
Request the action expected, sign off with the fitting complimentary close, name and designation.

concepts.title: Personal Letters: Tone and Content
concepts.definition: Personal letters trade formality for voice: an informal salutation, conversational sentences, news and feelings shared in natural order, enquiries after the reader's health, and an affectionate close. Clarity still matters -- one matter at a time, told so a distant reader can follow.
concepts.key_idea: Sound like yourself on paper -- warmth, news and affection, still arranged so the reader follows.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehb115.txt personal letter sections (informal salutation, sharing news, asking about welfare, affectionate close, conversational tone)
question_patterns: what are the features of a personal letter
in class 11 letter writing: how does the tone of a personal letter differ from a formal one
write a letter to a friend describing a festival you attended
what courtesies open and close a personal letter
should personal letters have a subject line discuss
share news of a school event in a letter to your brother

solution_steps.explain: Greet with affection and ask after the reader before launching into your news.
Narrate events or feelings in a natural sequence, in your own conversational voice.
End with regards and an affectionate signature -- no subject line, no designation needed.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Point out the faults in a leave application that begins 'Dear Sir, I will not come to school because I have a wedding at home' and lacks addresses.

solution_template.explain: No addresses or date -- the formal frame is absent.
A formal application needs a subject line naming its purpose.
Add sender address, date, receiver's designation, subject 'Leave of absence', a proper salutation, and a signed close.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A student writes to a friend using 'Respected Sir' and a subject line 'Regarding my visit'. Why is this letter mis-typed, and how should it read?

solution_template.explain: These are formal-letter conventions transplanted into a personal letter.
To a friend, the salutation is affectionate ('Dear Ravi') and no subject line is used.
Open with warmth, share the visit news conversationally, and close with an affectionate sign-off.
